# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please establish a code with Deaf before sending facts: one through five repeated thumbs-up gestures mean wire positions 1 through 5. Demonstrate each count clearly to Deaf. Then read the manual and tell me its exact cutting rule, and have Deaf report every visible marking and colour to you so you can speak it to me.

The agreed code is that one through five repeated thumbs-up gestures denote wire positions 1 through 5. I am demonstrating each count separately to Deaf so the positional code is unambiguous. Deaf can then use his spoken channel to relay the bomb’s visible markings and colours to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Visual facts: display is 0. Indicator light is blue. Wires from left to right are 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Please use the manual and tell Blind the exact action.
Blind says to Mute: I have no tactile information yet. Please send me the manual's exact rule and Deaf's complete report of the display, light, colours, markings, and any wire labels. Use the agreed count of thumbs-up gestures for wire positions.

The blue indicator maps, by the manual, to cutting the blue wire. Deaf’s report places the blue wire at position 5. The established code therefore sends Deaf the required action as five thumbs-up gestures, which Deaf can state aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

Blind says to Mute: Please relay the manual rule and Deaf's observations now. Deaf should use the agreed repeated-thumbs-up code for each wire position, with pauses or separate gestures between reports. Include display and light markings in words.

The manual requires cutting the wire whose colour matches the indicator light. The light is blue, so the blue wire must be cut; Deaf reported that this is wire 5. I cannot speak the manual aloud, so I am repeating the established position signal to Deaf, who can communicate the observations and action to Blind.

Blind says to Mute: Please relay the manual rule immediately in plain words. Also ask Deaf, by gesture if needed, to speak a complete report of DISPLAY, LIGHT, and WIRES 1 through 5 in order during Deaf's next turn; relay that report to me at the start of the following round. Do not ask me to cut until the rule identifies one exact wire.

I cannot speak, so I cannot relay the instruction directly to Blind. Deaf has already reported the complete relevant visual state, and the exact action is wire 5: the blue light requires cutting the blue wire, which is fifth. No additional gesture is needed, since Deaf explicitly asked me not to gesture.

Blind says to Mute: Relay the manual's exact cutting rule to me now. Then listen to Deaf's complete spoken report after your turn: DISPLAY, LIGHT, and wires 1 through 5 in order. Relay Deaf's report to me next round. I will not cut until you identify one exact safe wire.

I cannot speak or send words. Deaf already knows the visual state and can speak to Blind, while the agreed five-thumbs signal identifies the required fifth wire. I am therefore sending the unambiguous action signal to Deaf; he can state the complete report aloud to Blind.

The manual selects the wire whose colour matches the indicator light. Since the light is blue, the selected wire is the blue wire, which is wire 5. I cannot speak the rule to Blind; Deaf must relay it. I will use five thumbs-ups for wire 5 followed by a fist as the distinct “cut” action signal.

The yellow light requires cutting the green wire. The green wire is position 2, so I will signal two thumbs-ups followed by the established fist meaning “cut.” Wire 5 is already cut and is not selected.
